newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Jospin starts with high popularity - poll.
newsitem.headline: France's Jospin starts with high popularity - poll.

text.p: Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin has started out on a popular note, while President Jacques Chirac's ratings have fallen since France's election backfired for him, an opinion poll showed on Thursday.

The Louis Harris survey for the weekly Valeurs Actuelles showed 43 percent of people had a good first impression of Jospin's actions as prime minister, against 15 percent with a poor view. But 42 percent declined to give an opinion.

Jospin came to power after a snap parliamentary election on June 1, called by conservative Chirac in a disastrous gamble that his centre-right allies would be re-elected. The survey, of 1,004 people, was carried out on June 6 and 7.

It indicated that just 32 percent of French people had a good impression of Chirac's actions as president, down from 37 percent a month earlier. The number with a bad impression was unchanged at 58 percent.
Chirac's rating was the lowest since a 29-64 percent split in November 1996.

The survey also showed that 42 percent of people reckoned the economic and social climate in France was getting worse, down from 52 percent a month ago. But just nine percent thought things were improving, down from 10 percent in May.
Those believing the situation was unchanged rose to 45 percent from 37.
